Hi Joe —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m capturing the acceptance criteria and a proposed validation / cutover cadence so we have a single reference ahead of the swap. Please review and confirm the items below or flag any missing constraints from your infra side.

Acceptance and validation summary (proposed):
- Throughput target: 120 req/s sustained, 220 req/s burst for the 95th percentile user profile.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 750ms for 512-token gen.
- Fault tolerance: automatic fallback to hosted model (same model family,cpu fallback) for 5% degraded nodes.
- KV/prefix cache: customer prefix-hit-rate target >= 70% to meet token-cost objectives.

Validation cadence (proposed):
1) Week-of dry run: synthesis test with your anonymized load-profile (attached) on dedicated staging.
2) Stress window: 3-hour ramp to 1.5x expected peak to validate autoscale and queuing behavior.
3) Canary: 1% production traffic routed to dedicated for 24 hours.
4) Full swap: scheduled 2-hour blackout window for stateful cutover, followed by 4-hour sanity readout.

Blackout windows: we recommend a 2-hour maintenance window during your low-traffic window. We’ve tentatively proposed Friday 2026-06-25 02:00-04:00 UTC (local Friday afternoon for Novus operations).

Attached: load-profile.csv (de-identified user traffic samples).

Next steps: please confirm (a) the blackout window works for Novus ops, (b) we can get a signed mutual action plan (MAP) by Thursday EOD, and (c) whether you want Redwood to run the stress window or if you’ll execute it from your side.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Looping in ops plan and owners. High level runbook that I’ll action once Novus confirms blackout window:

1) Preflight (T-72 to T-24):
   - Validate model artifact parity (hashes) between hosted and dedicated. Owner: Karthik.
   - Reserve dedicated capacity: 8 x A100-equivalent for smoke; scale to 14 x A100-equivalent during stress window. Owner: Infra oncall.
   - Confirm KV cache warmers and prefix cache warm rates. Owner: Sean.

2) Dry run (T-24):
   - Redwood runs load using the attached MAP-v1 doc parameters (simulated user mix + ramp). We’ll collect token-level breakdown, GPU utilization, and tail-latency traces.
   - Success gate: p95 latency within 1.2x hosted baseline and no queue saturation > 15s.

3) Stress window (T-12):
   - 3-hour ramp to 1.5x expected peak. Redwood leads.

4) Canary (T-6):
   - 1% of production traffic to dedicated for 24h. Monitoring hooks and automatic rollback policy in HubSpot ticket.

5) Swap (T-0):
   - 2-hour blackout for stateful KV persistence flush and DNS cutover. Post-cutover 4-hour sanity readout. If any gate fails, auto-fallback to hosted.

I’ve attached the working MAP draft — please review and I’ll push to Drive for DocuSign routing.

Sean
